stories.body: At least 13 people were killed after a powerful earthquake struck Kumamoto prefecture on Japan's southern island of Kyushu on Tuesday. Rescue crews are searching damaged sites including an Aeon shopping mall, where an explosion followed the quake and people were reported missing, and a paper mill in Yatsushiro, where a collapsed chimney trapped workers. The quake was initially measured at magnitude 7.1 before the US Geological Survey revised its estimate to 6.8; it registered the maximum level of 7 on Japan's intensity scale. Thousands of people have taken shelter in evacuation centres, while power and water outages have affected large numbers of households. Authorities have warned of further strong aftershocks and landslides in the coming days.
stories.headline: Japan earthquake death toll rises to 13 as rescuers search collapsed sites

stories.body: The United States and Saudi Arabia said they carried out joint strikes on logistics and weapons sites used by Iran-aligned militias in eastern Iraq, following drone attacks on US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure. Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces, an umbrella organisation that includes Iran-backed militias and is formally part of the country's security forces, said at least 20 members were killed and 32 wounded in strikes across several provinces. Iraq's presidency condemned the attacks as a violation of sovereignty, while Iran also denounced them. The strikes followed an Iranian missile attack that US Central Command said was intercepted, ending a brief lull in the wider regional conflict.
stories.headline: US and Saudi forces strike Iran-aligned groups in Iraq amid renewed escalation

stories.body: Iran has rejected an Oman-backed Gulf proposal to jointly manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and is seeking partial control over an Omani shipping route, according to reports. The proposal reportedly included voluntary fees for vessels using the strategic waterway and was intended to restore stable commercial shipping after months of disruption linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran and attacks on vessels. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical global energy transit route, and the dispute comes amid renewed military escalation in the region.
stories.headline: Iran rejects Omani proposal for joint management of Strait of Hormuz shipping

stories.body: Firefighters in France's Gironde region are working to contain wildfires near Bordeaux as another heatwave is expected to bring temperatures near 40C. Authorities reported new flare-ups in areas already affected by the fires and evacuated nearly 4,000 people from tourist accommodation around Lacanau on the Atlantic coast because of the risk of a renewed spread. The Gironde fire has burned about 42,000 hectares, while other major fires have affected France, Spain and Italy. In Spain, some evacuation orders have been lifted, but officials warn that high temperatures, wind and dry conditions could worsen fires again.
stories.headline: Wildfires threaten southwest France again as a new heatwave approaches

stories.body: Colt Gray, the teenager who pleaded guilty last week to a 2024 shooting rampage at a high school outside Atlanta that killed four people, has been sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
stories.headline: Georgia teenager who killed four people in a school shooting is sentenced to life without parole

stories.body: Police believe two suspects were shooting at each other when gunfire erupted at the Bite of Seattle food festival near the Space Needle, killing three people and injuring at least four others, including a toddler. A 15-year-old suspect has been arrested and was reportedly armed with a ghost gun, while police were still seeking another suspect. Authorities said there was no continuing threat to the public, and the investigation was examining whether the shooting was gang-related.
stories.headline: Seattle food-festival shooting that killed three may have been gang-related

stories.body: A tornado swept through northeastern Wisconsin on Monday, damaging homes and businesses, overturning vehicles, downing trees and power lines, and knocking out electricity to more than 30,000 people. The National Weather Service confirmed a tornado in Winnebago County, affecting the Fox Cities area including Appleton, Menasha and Neenah. Workers and residents sheltered as the midday storm passed, and volunteers began clearing debris the following day.
stories.headline: Wisconsin tornado causes widespread damage and power outages

stories.body: Haitian immigrants with Temporary Protected Status and their employers are facing uncertainty after the Trump administration's termination of the programme took effect. The decision affects about 350,000 Haitians who had been living and working legally in the United States, including many who have held jobs for more than a decade. The Supreme Court allowed the administration to end TPS on June 25 after challenges in lower courts, leaving businesses to determine whether workers can remain on their payrolls and exposing affected migrants to possible deportation.
stories.headline: Thousands of Haitian immigrants and US employers face confusion over lost work authorization

stories.body: Spain's cabinet has partially pardoned Laura Borràs, the former speaker of Catalonia's parliament, reducing her prison sentence from four years, six months and one day to two years and thereby avoiding her imprisonment. Her fine and lengthy disqualification from public office remain in force. Borràs was convicted of administrative misconduct and document forgery for splitting contracts and awarding them to an associate while she led the Institution of Catalan Letters. The government said it followed the recommendation of the Catalan High Court of Justice, which had found the original prison term disproportionate.
stories.headline: Spain partially pardons former Catalan parliament speaker Laura Borràs

stories.body: Firefighters have stabilised major wildfires in Madrid and Ávila after they burned more than 75,000 hectares, allowing many evacuees to return home, although some restrictions remain. Elsewhere, a fire at La Vall d'Uixó in Castellón has burned nearly 10,000 hectares, remains active and has forced the evacuation of about 10,000 residents. New serious fires have also emerged in Castilla y León, including one near the Arribes del Duero natural park in Zamora. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Spain faces a critical and complex situation because high temperatures, low humidity and wind are aiding the spread of fires.
stories.headline: Spain's wildfires ease in some areas, but major fires and heat still threaten communities

stories.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has renewed his call for a national pact on climate change and wildfire prevention as major fires affect communities across Spain, but the conservative People's Party has rejected opening negotiations with his government. The two sides say they support institutional coordination and emergency resources, but disagree over responsibility, prevention and the terms of any long-term agreement. The government has declared areas affected by 211 catastrophic incidents, mostly wildfires, eligible for civil-protection aid, and says more than 170,000 hectares have burned so far this year.
stories.headline: Spain's government and opposition remain divided over proposed climate pact after wildfires

stories.body: Spain's Education Ministry says technical staff detected during the 2025 PISA testing process that too many students were being exempted in Catalonia, but the warning was not passed to senior officials in either the national or regional administration. Catalonia's final exemption rate reached 23.2%, far above the OECD's 5% limit, leading the OECD to exclude the region's results from international comparisons. The ministry says it did not learn of the eventual consequences until March 2026, while the Catalan government says it also only became aware of the issue then and is continuing its internal investigation.
stories.headline: Questions grow over exclusion of students from Catalonia's PISA assessments

stories.body: Mossos d'Esquadra have arrested a man in connection with the violent death of a 34-year-old woman at a home in Barcelona's Sant Martí district. Police are treating the case as a suspected gender-based killing. Officers responded to a report of an assault on Tuesday evening and found the woman seriously injured; emergency workers later confirmed her death. Reports said children may have been present and that the suspect fled before being detained, while investigators continue to establish the circumstances.
stories.headline: Police investigate killing of woman in Barcelona as suspected gender-based violence

stories.body: Catalonia's unemployment rate fell to 7.9% in the second quarter of 2026, dropping below 8% for the first second quarter since 2008, according to Spain's Labour Force Survey. The number of unemployed people declined by 92,600 from the previous quarter to 343,000, while employment rose to a record 3.9978 million people. Job growth was strongest in services during the tourist season, followed by industry and construction. Youth unemployment also declined, though it remained higher than for older age groups, and temporary employment grew faster than permanent employment.
stories.headline: Catalonia's unemployment rate falls below 8% in the second quarter

stories.body: Catalonia's Education Department, employer groups and unions representing publicly funded private schools have signed a €118 million agreement to improve teachers' working conditions over the five school years from 2026 to 2031. The plan will gradually reduce teaching hours, beginning with a two-hour reduction for teachers over 58 in 2026-27 and later extending reductions across primary and secondary education. It will also improve cover for medical absences by requiring replacements from the seventh day of leave rather than the 16th day, and includes better pay for some additional responsibilities.
stories.headline: Catalonia agrees €118 million plan to improve conditions for publicly funded private-school teachers

stories.body: Barcelona Metro operator TMB is investigating whether a lining installed near the overhead electrical system during Glòries-area construction caused a fire in an L1 tunnel between Clot and Glòries. TMB says the material, intended to waterproof that part of the tunnel, exists nowhere else on the network. The driver stopped the train after seeing smoke and flames, but passengers opened emergency door releases before the train could reverse to Clot station, allowing smoke into the carriages and prompting an evacuation along the tracks. More than 100 people were treated for smoke inhalation, and the line resumed normal service the following morning.
stories.headline: Barcelona Metro investigates whether unique tunnel lining caused L1 fire
